Sample Size Planning From the AIPE Perspective for a Mean Under Two-Phase Sampling

Source: R/ss_aipe_two_phase.R
ss_aipe_two_phase.Rd

Plans the number of labeled units, \(n\), on which a costly target measurement must be taken so that the confidence interval for the target mean from ci_two_phase is sufficiently narrow, when an inexpensive proxy measurement is available on every unit of a pool of \(M\) units. The plan follows the accuracy in parameter estimation (AIPE) approach: the goal is an interval no wider than width, either at the planning values (the expected width) or with a stated assurance that the realized interval will be that narrow (Kelley & Rausch, 2006). Beside the answer it reports the number of labeled units the same goal needs without the proxy, so the saving is in view.

Usage

ss_aipe_two_phase(
  true_sd_Y,
  true_cor,
  width,
  n_pool = Inf,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  assurance = NULL,
  true_kurtosis = 0
)

Arguments

true_sd_Y

Planning value of the standard deviation of the target measurement, \(\sigma_Y\).

true_cor

Planning value of the correlation between the target and the proxy, \(\rho\).

width

The desired full width of the confidence interval (the upper limit minus the lower limit), in the units of the target.

n_pool

The number of units in the pool, \(M\), every one of which carries the proxy. The default Inf plans as though the pool were unlimited.

conf_level

Confidence level (default 0.95).

assurance

NULL (default) to plan for the expected width, or a probability in (0, 1) that the realized width will be no wider than width, as in ss_aipe_c.

true_kurtosis

Excess kurtosis (the scale of kurtosis) of the residual of the target on the proxy; default 0, its normal value. Used only with assurance, where it adjusts the degrees of freedom of the variance estimate (see Details).

Value

A data.frame (classes dmar_ss_aipe and dmar_tbl) with rows

necessary_n_labeled

the planned number of labeled units.

necessary_n_target_only

the number the same goal needs without the proxy.

ratio

the first divided by the second.

expected_width

the full width at necessary_n_labeled and the planning values.

minimum_width

the narrowest width the pool allows, the normal-quantile width with all but one unit of the pool labeled (0 for an unlimited pool; see Details).

width, true_sd_Y, true_cor, n_pool, conf_level

the inputs.

assurance, true_kurtosis

the inputs, present only when an assurance was supplied.

Details

The interval planned for. The regression estimator of double sampling (Tamhane, 1978, Section 2.1, p. 420; the design is that of Neyman, 1938, who formed strata from the inexpensive variable) that ci_two_phase reports has, to first order, variance \(\sigma_Y^2(1 - \rho^2)/n + \rho^2\sigma_Y^2/M\), and its interval uses the t distribution on \(n - 2\) degrees of freedom. With \(\omega\) the desired width (width), \(1 - \alpha\) the conf_level, and \(t_n = t_{1-\alpha/2,\, n-2}\), the plan for the expected width is the smallest \(n\) with $$2\, t_n \left\{\frac{\sigma_Y^2(1 - \rho^2)}{n} + \frac{\rho^2\sigma_Y^2}{M}\right\}^{1/2} \le \omega.$$ In an evaluation of a system whose outputs an automated judge labels, for example, \(n\) is the number of outputs a human assessor must label when the judge has labeled \(M\) of them.

Assurance. The realized width replaces \(\sigma_Y^2(1 - \rho^2)\) by the residual mean square \(S_e^2\) and \(\rho^2 \sigma_Y^2\) by \(\hat b^2 S_X^2\). Treating the second, which is divided by the large \(M\), as fixed at its planning value, and \(\nu S_e^2 / \sigma_e^2\) as chi square on \(\nu\) degrees of freedom, the probability that the realized width is at most \(\omega\) is $$F_{\chi^2_\nu}\left(\frac{\nu\, n\, \{\omega^2 / (4 t_n^2) - \rho^2 \sigma_Y^2 / M\}}{\sigma_Y^2 (1 - \rho^2)}\right),$$ and the plan is the smallest \(n\) from which it is at least assurance at every larger \(n\). Under normal residuals \(\nu = n - 2\). For residuals with excess kurtosis \(\kappa\) (true_kurtosis) the variance of \(S_e^2\) is approximately \(\sigma_e^4\{2/(n - 2) + \kappa/n\}\), and matching it to a scaled chi square gives \(\nu = 2 / \{2/(n - 2) + \kappa/n\}\): for an assurance of .80 or more, a lighter-tailed residual (\(\kappa < 0\)) needs fewer units and a heavier-tailed one more. A binary target is not light-tailed as a rule: a 0/1 variable with proportion \(p\) has excess kurtosis \(\{1 - 6p(1 - p)\}/\{p(1 - p)\}\), which is negative only for \(p\) between about .21 and .79 and is about 5.1 at \(p = .90\). The planning value is best taken from the residuals of a pilot regression of the target on the proxy, through kurtosis. With a large \(\kappa\) and a small \(n\), \(\nu\) is small, and the two-moment approximation can reach the assurance at a few small \(n\), fall below it over a stretch of larger ones, and reach it again; the plan is the start of the stretch over which it holds for good, which the search finds exactly for any assurance in (0, 1). Under normal residuals and with an assurance of one half or more the two readings agree.

The pool sets a floor. The labeled units are drawn from the pool, and ci_two_phase needs at least one unit that carries the proxy alone, so \(n \le M - 1\). No number of labeled units can therefore bring the width below \(2 z_{1-\alpha/2} \{\sigma_Y^2(1 - \rho^2)/(M - 1) + \rho^2\sigma_Y^2/M\}^{1/2}\) (the minimum_width row), which is close to \(2 z_{1-\alpha/2}\, \sigma_Y / \sqrt{M}\), the width of the target mean were every unit of the pool labeled; a target at or below it is an error. A target just above it can still be out of reach once the t quantile and the assurance are accounted for; when the plan needs more than \(M - 1\) labeled units, that too is an error, naming the pool as the constraint, rather than a missing value.

The target-only comparison. necessary_n_target_only is the planned size of the usual t interval for the target mean from labeled units alone, the plan ss_aipe_mean() makes for a single mean, so the two functions agree. Without an assurance it is the smallest \(n\) with \(2\, t_{1-\alpha/2,\, n-1}\, c_4(n)\, \sigma_Y / \sqrt{n} \le \omega\), where \(c_4(n)\sigma_Y\) is the expected sample standard deviation under normality, so that the left side is the exact expected width; with assurance it is the same chi square argument on \(n - 1\) degrees of freedom. It is not bounded by n_pool, because a design without the proxy has no use for a pool. The true_kurtosis supplied is the residual's, and the comparison uses it for the target as well, an approximation: the target's own kurtosis can differ, and the comparison for it is ss_aipe_mean() with that value. The labeled-unit plan, by contrast, sets the two estimates in its standard error at their planning values, since the expected value of the two-phase standard error has no closed form once the pool term enters; this overstates its expected width slightly, by a factor of at most about \(1 + 1/\{4(n - 2)\}\), and can add a unit to necessary_n_labeled.

References

Kelley, K., & Rausch, J. R. (2006). Sample size planning for the standardized mean difference: Accuracy in parameter estimation via narrow confidence intervals. Psychological Methods, 11(4), 363–385. doi:10.1037/1082-989X.11.4.363

Neyman, J. (1938). Contribution to the theory of sampling human populations. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 33(201), 101–116. doi:10.1080/01621459.1938.10503378

Tamhane, A. C. (1978). Inference based on regression estimator in double sampling. Biometrika, 65(2), 419–427. doi:10.1093/biomet/65.2.419

ci_two_phase for the interval, ss_aipe_two_phase_cost for the least costly numbers of labeled and pool units, ss_aipe_two_phase_sensitivity to evaluate a plan by simulation, and ss_seq_two_phase for the sequential rule.

Examples

# Planning values from a pilot: a target standard deviation of 0.43 and
# a correlation of 0.55 with the proxy, which is available on a pool of
# 20,000 units. A 90% interval no wider than 0.10:
ss_aipe_two_phase(true_sd_Y = 0.43, true_cor = 0.55, width = 0.10,
                  n_pool = 20000,
                  conf_level = 0.90)
#>  term                    value
#>  necessary_n_labeled     142  
#>  necessary_n_target_only 202  
#>  ratio                   0.703
#>  expected_width          0.100
#>  minimum_width           0.010
#>  width                   0.100
#>  true_sd_Y               0.430
#>  true_cor                0.550
#>  n_pool                  20000
#>  conf_level              0.900
#> 
#> Confidence level: 90%

# The same goal with 80% assurance that the realized interval is no
# wider than 0.10:
ss_aipe_two_phase(true_sd_Y = 0.43, true_cor = 0.55, width = 0.10,
                  n_pool = 20000,
                  conf_level = 0.90, assurance = 0.80)
#>  term                    value
#>  necessary_n_labeled     156  
#>  necessary_n_target_only 218  
#>  ratio                   0.716
#>  expected_width          0.095
#>  minimum_width           0.010
#>  width                   0.100
#>  true_sd_Y               0.430
#>  true_cor                0.550
#>  n_pool                  20000
#>  conf_level              0.900
#>  assurance               0.800
#>  true_kurtosis           0.000
#> 
#> Confidence level: 90%

# A smaller pool raises the floor and the number of labeled units.
ss_aipe_two_phase(true_sd_Y = 0.43, true_cor = 0.55, width = 0.10,
                  n_pool = 1000,
                  conf_level = 0.90, assurance = 0.80)
#>  term                    value
#>  necessary_n_labeled     165  
#>  necessary_n_target_only 218  
#>  ratio                   0.757
#>  expected_width          0.096
#>  minimum_width           0.045
#>  width                   0.100
#>  true_sd_Y               0.430
#>  true_cor                0.550
#>  n_pool                  1000 
#>  conf_level              0.900
#>  assurance               0.800
#>  true_kurtosis           0.000
#> 
#> Confidence level: 90%
